question: For successful fitting of a patellar tendon-bearing (PTB) prosthetic socket in a transtibial amputee, the ideal stump should be cylindrical rather than conical, because a conical stump migrates distally within the socket and causes skin breakdown at the stump tip.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The PTB socket is designed for cylindrical stumps. Conical stumps taper and migrate distally within the socket, causing stump-tip pressure sores. This is why post-operative stump bandaging uses a figure-of-eight technique that shapes the stump into a cylinder from day one.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A cylindrical stump distributes load evenly across the PTB socket. A conical stump (tapered distally) slides down into the socket, concentrating pressure at the distal end-bearing surface and causing ulceration — a leading cause of prosthetic non-use in Indian amputees.
